svg.title: Normal spatial states and reducing pieces cannot match the internally flipped join
svg.desc: For commuting semifinite type II factors generating M and exchanged by an internal self-adjoint involution, either normal-state agreement or a nonzero bounded intertwiner would force a normal spatial multiplication isomorphism. Its finite corner would contain the impossible diffuse flip. This leaves other nonspatial pairs open.
svg.text: Normal spatial states cannot match this actual join.
P,Q: type II factors · P,Q commute · M = P ∨ Q is a factor · S = S* ∈ M · S² = 1 · SPS = Q
Path A: normal states ψ on M and Ω on P ⊗̄ Q agree.
Ω(a ⊗ b) = ψ(ab) for every a ∈ P, b ∈ Q · (5E.1)
Their GNS cross terms agree: V[Σ aᵢ ⊗ bᵢ]Ω = [Σ aᵢbᵢ]ψ.
Normal factor representations are faithful; joint generation makes V onto.
Ω may be entangled; neither state needs to be faithful · Lemma 5E.1, (5E.2)–(5E.4)
Path B: a nonzero T intertwines normal θ and π.
Tθ(a ⊗ b) = π(ab)T · T = U|T| · (5E.5)
e = supp|T| ∈ θ(P ⊗̄ Q)′; f = supp|T*| ∈ π(M)′ · (5E.6)
U: eK → fH is unitary; both restricted normal representations are faithful.
The supports reduce the full images because the two copies jointly generate · Proposition 5E.3
Either path gives the normal multiplication isomorphism P ⊗̄ Q ≅ M.
Transport S; compress to p ⊗ SpS with p intrinsically finite and nonzero.
Proposition 5D.3 and Lemma 5C.2 forbid the finite spatial flip.
No normal-state agreement, and T = 0 for every such intertwiner.
Theorem 5E.2 · Proposition 5E.3 · joint generation is essential.
A full candidate must be constructed in a nonspatial position.
These obstructions leave the unrestricted other-pair existence question open.
Human-source target: Connes, Corollary 11 and Sakai note, author PDF 44–45.
